title: Transparent node quarantine & reintegration workflow for emergency maintenance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated fleets occasionally need emergency intervention (disk corruption, thermal events, driver crashes). Today we perform node drains that immediately stop new allocations and begin evicting in-flight work. This results in abrupt throughput drops and frequent safety-fallbacks (model variant fallbacks or cross-region failovers) that increase latency and cost for customers.

Goal:
Introduce a transparent, low-latency "quarantine" lifecycle state that isolates a node from new allocations while allowing in-flight requests and KV caches to complete under controlled conditions, and then provide an automated reintegration path that warms caches and ramps traffic back. The flow should minimize customer-visible SLO violations during emergency maintenance and reduce unnecessary model fallbacks.

Design overview (high level):
- New node lifecycle states: Active -> Quarantine -> Draining -> Isolated -> Reintegrating -> Active. Quarantine is a soft-isolation state that prevents new model allocations but preserves accepted requests and cache affinity. Reintegrating performs health checks and staged traffic ramp.
- Quarantine policy parameters: max-quarantine-duration, soft-allocation-backpressure (reject new allocations only if capacity headroom < threshold), grace-window-per-model (longer for long-lived KV-heavy models).
- Autoscaler integration: Quarantine reduces available capacity for scheduling decisions without triggering immediate scale-up. The autoscaler will consider quarantined nodes as warm capacity candidate for short-term reuse if within reintegration window.
- Throughput guarantees: tie quarantine policies to tenant throughput reservations. If quarantining risks dropping committed throughput, the policy will either (a) delay quarantine, (b) trigger prioritized rebalancing from lower-priority workloads, or (c) initiate controlled cross-pool shift per running policy.
- Reintegration: staged ballot of health checks (GPU memory checks, kernel readiness, KV cache hit ratio warm-up) and a traffic ramp schedule (10% -> 33% -> 66% -> 100) with observation windows. Reintegrated nodes advertise readiness only after warm-up thresholds met.
- Observability & control: Console UI to visualize quarantined nodes, timeline, expected reintegration ETA, and an operator fast-path to force-isolate or abort reintegration. Metrics: quarantined_node_count, avg_quarantine_duration, reintegration_success_rate, customer_throughput_loss.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spec and API: Define node lifecycle state machine, new cluster API flags, and quota interactions. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DF/Node+Quarantine+Spec)
2) Runtime: Implement state transitions in node agent + scheduler hooks. Add soft-allocation filter.
3) Autoscaler: Update decision logic to treat quarantined nodes as "soft unavailable" and add threshold override hooks for throughput-reserved customers.
4) Console/UI: Add quarantined node list, reintegration controls, and per-node audit trail.
5) Telemetry: Dashboards and alerts (Grafana dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/maintenance/quarantine)
6) Testing & rollout: Unit tests, integration tests with dedicated workload harness, canary rollout to a single region, then progressive ramp.

Acceptance criteria:
- New node lifecycle state machine implemented and unit-tested.
- Quarantine state prevents new allocations but allows existing requests to complete; validated by end-to-end integration test with KV-heavy model (latency/throughput preserved within SLO for 95% of requests during simulated quarantine events).
- Reintegration path performs health checks and staged ramp; reintegration success rate >= 98% in canary region.
- Autoscaler does not trigger unnecessary large-scale provisioning in response to quarantines for short (<10m) events for non-reserved tenants.
- Console displays quarantined nodes with operator controls; audit trail stores transition events for 30 days.
- Documentation and runbook published (link in Confluence).

Rollout & risk mitigation:
- Canary to us-west-1 dedicated pool for 48h with synthetic KV workloads and real customer night-window traffic. Monitor throughput loss and fallback events.
- Add kill-switch feature: controller-level env var to disable reintegration auto-ramp if regression observed.

Metrics to monitor post-launch:
- quarantined_node_count, avg_quarantine_duration, reintegration_success_rate, impacted_customers_count, fallback_triggered_count, median_recovery_time
comments: 2026-02-16 — Aisha Patel: Initial triage completed. Root-cause patterns point to increased thermal events and occasional driver-level hangs; current immediate-drain behavior amplifies customer impact.
2026-02-18 — Marco Ruiz: Drafted state-machine and parameter list. Added soft-allocation-backpressure idea to avoid immediate capacity shock.
2026-02-22 — Design review (Lina Cho): Approved UI mockups for quarantined node timeline; requested operator ability to tag quarantine reason.
2026-02-25 — PM review (Ravi Menon): Flagged interaction with throughput guarantees; asked to add explicit decision tree for reserved tenants vs best-effort tenants.
2026-02-28 — ENG PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2897 — implements node state transitions and agent hooks. Needs integration tests for autoscaler behavior.

2026-03-01 — Integration test results: quarantine allowed KV flows to drain, but observed a reintegration race where cache warm-up delayed service for 2 nodes. We will add a 'cold-cache detection' gate before announcing readiness.
2026-03-02 — Marco Ruiz: Updated acceptance criteria and trial canary window to include cold-cache detection gate. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-05 in us-west-1.
2026-03-02 — Action items: (1) Add telemetry for 'reintegration_warmup_seconds' (2) Add e2e scenario with throughput-reserved tenant to ensure we don't violate guarantees.
